question: Can a Route 53 Profile be shared across AWS Regions?

claim: If your organization prefers to allow all outbound DNS lookups by default and only needs to block known malicious domains, you can use DNS Firewall to create denylists of the malicious domain names you know.
question: How can DNS Firewall block only known malicious domains and allow everything else?

evidence.quote: (2) If your organization prefers to allow all outbound DNS lookups within your accounts by default and only requires the ability to block DNS requests for known malicious domains, you can use DNS Firewall to create denylists, which include all the malicious domain names your organization is aware of.

claim: DNS Firewall complements other AWS network and application security services by giving control and visibility over Route 53 Resolver DNS traffic (such as AmazonProvidedDNS) for the entire VPC.
question: What traffic does DNS Firewall give control and visibility over?

evidence.quote: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall complements existing network and application security services on AWS by providing control and visibility to Route 53 Resolver DNS traffic (e.g. AmazonProvidedDNS) for your entire VPC.

claim: DNS Firewall works together with AWS Firewall Manager, so you can build policies based on DNS Firewall rules and apply them centrally across your VPCs and accounts.
question: Which service lets you apply DNS Firewall policies centrally across VPCs and accounts?

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall works together with AWS Firewall Manager so you can build policies based on DNS Firewall rules, and then centrally apply those policies across your VPCs and accounts.

claim: Amazon Route 53 Global Resolver is reachable over the internet with encrypted DNS queries (DoH or DoT), while the Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver is the default regional resolver for VPCs, reachable from the VPC or over private connections using Resolver endpoints.
question: What is the difference between Route 53 Global Resolver and VPC Resolver?

values.display: Default regional resolver for Amazon VPCs

qualifiers.condition: Global Resolver is not examined; support for the comparison only

evidence.quote: Route 53 Global Resolver: Global Resolver that is reachable over the internet with encryption of DNS queries in transit (DoH or DoT).
Route 53 VPC Resolver : Default regional resolver for Amazon VPCs and reachable by clients hosted in the VPC, or by clients over private connections (VPN or Direct Connect) using Resolver endpoints.

claim: Make sure your domain name registrar uses the name servers of your Amazon Route 53 hosted zone; if not, Route 53 is not authoritative for queries to your domain.
question: Why might Route 53 not be authoritative for a domain even though a hosted zone exists?

values.display: will not be authoritative for queries to your domain

evidence.quote: You should also make sure that your domain name registrar is using the name servers in your Amazon Route 53 hosted zone.
If not, Amazon Route 53 will not be authoritative for queries to your domain.

claim: Amazon Route 53 provides highly available and scalable DNS, domain name registration and health-checking web services.
question: What is Amazon Route 53?

values.display: highly available and scalable Domain Name System (DNS)

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 provides highly available and scalable Domain Name System (DNS), domain name registration, and health-checking web services.

claim: Amazon Route 53 connects user requests to infrastructure running in AWS, such as EC2 instances, load balancers or S3 buckets, and can also route users to infrastructure outside of AWS.
question: Can Route 53 route users to infrastructure outside AWS?

evidence.quote: Route 53 effectively connects user requests to infrastructure running in AWS – such as Amazon EC2 instances, Elastic Load Balancing load balancers, or Amazon S3 buckets – and can also be used to route users to infrastructure outside of AWS.

claim: DNS is a globally distributed service that translates human readable names into the numeric IP addresses that computers use to connect to each other.
question: What does a Domain Name System (DNS) service do?

evidence.quote: DNS is a globally distributed service that translates human readable names like www.example.com into the numeric IP addresses like 192.0.2.1 that computers use to connect to each other.

claim: When you register a new domain name with Amazon Route 53, it automatically creates a hosted zone that stores the DNS records for the domain.
question: Does registering a domain in Route 53 also create a hosted zone?

evidence.quote: Route 53 automatically creates a hosted zone that stores DNS records for your domain.

claim: If your domain name is not managed by Amazon Route 53, you must tell the registrar to update the domain's name servers to the ones associated with your hosted zone.
question: What must you do at the registrar when a domain is registered elsewhere but its DNS is in Route 53?

values.display: update the name servers for your domain

evidence.quote: If your domain name is not managed by Route 53, you will need to inform the registrar with whom you registered your domain name to update the name servers for your domain to the ones associated with your hosted zone.
